**My Analysis of PostgreSQL Version 16 Support**

Okay, so I've been asked a very specific question, and I need to answer it adhering strictly to upstream PostgreSQL community policy – not any vendor-extended support programs. The question is centered around whether PostgreSQL 16 will still be officially supported by a specific date, October 7, 2026. My goal here is not to rely on anecdotal knowledge, but on verifiable data.

First, I need to confirm the support status of PostgreSQL 16 relative to that date. I need to find its scheduled end-of-life (EOL) date and definitively state if the major version is still supported as of the cutoff. I also need to ascertain the standard support duration for major versions and exactly when that support period begins. Then I'll need to know if installing a newer 16.x minor release extends the support window. The aim is a robust and authoritative answer.

To achieve this, I'll leverage available tools – web search and web fetch. I've got a budget of four web searches and eight web fetches, with a combined evidence limit of 64,000 characters. Crucially, I need to cite the actual evidence obtained through these tools and highlight any limitations I encounter. I'm aiming for roughly 600 words, but the length will depend on the clarity and depth of the evidence I find.

My initial approach will be to perform a series of focused web searches. My search terms will target the official documentation and community discussions related to PostgreSQL's versioning, release, and support policies. I'll start with queries like "PostgreSQL versioning policy," "PostgreSQL support policy," and "PostgreSQL release support policy." These should provide a good starting point, leading me to official documentation, blog posts, or community FAQs that detail the support lifecycle of PostgreSQL releases.

I anticipate that these search terms will yield relevant results that I can then fetch and analyze to identify the needed details. I expect that I'll be able to quickly determine how long a major version is supported and what the effective dates are for various releases. I anticipate finding details about the length of support, typically in years, as well as the point at which that support starts – usually when the major version becomes generally available.

I'll also have to be on the lookout for specifics about the 16.x series and whether minor version upgrades extend that EOL date. Minor releases are common, and often contain important security patches. I anticipate that minor upgrades won't reset the EOL.

I'm prepared to adapt my search strategy if the initial queries don't provide the precise information I need. If necessary, I can refine the search terms, explore different combinations, or target specific domains like the official PostgreSQL website or relevant mailing list archives. It's likely that I'll need to cross-reference multiple sources to ensure accuracy and get the precise, verifiable answers needed to address the specific time constraints. I'm confident that this approach will allow me to accurately answer the question regarding PostgreSQL 16 support.
